articles.title: Hanford Cleanup: DOE’s Plans to Grout and Dispose of Millions of Gallons of Tank Waste
articles.snippet:
What GAO Found

The Department of Energy (DOE) is pursuing options to grout (i.e., immobilize in a concrete-like mixture) a portion of waste from 22 underground storage tanks at the Hanford Site. Specifically, DOE plans to grout about 24 million gallons of waste that has low levels of radioactivity—called low-activity waste (LAW). articles.title: Nuclear Waste Cleanup: DOE Shortages in Mission-Critical Positions Have Continued to Increase
articles.snippet:
What GAO Found

The Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Environmental Management (EM) has become further understaffed since GAO reported on EM’s workforce challenges in July 2024. From fiscal year (FY) 2023 through FY 2025, total staff decreased by 33 percent, from 1,272 to 856. This created an overall vacancy rate of 45 percent as of the end of FY 2025, based on a staffing need of 1,515 full-time employees that EM identified in FY 2023.

articles.snippet: Broken workflows and broken data pipelines will lead to biased AI and bad AI design, according to  Dr. Deepti Pandita, CMIO and chief AI officer at the University of California Irvine.  That’s why having an informaticist and a practicing physician who is cognizant of workflow design in the AI systems is important, said Pandita, who is both and who has a center seat on AI decisions at UCI.  “If you let the AI systems dictate what follows in terms of workflow or implementation, they are very likely to fail,” Pandita said.
